A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work, with matching authors, core results, and Appendices A and B. All pages, equations, and appendix proofs are readable and support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports theoretical results and proofs, including in both appendices. Empirical claims about FLIPD, including negative dimension estimates, are attributed to prior work.

after.justification: v2 remains theoretical. Its added literature discussion and references to earlier empirical results do not report original experiments, simulations, or data analyses.

M1.justification: The diffusion formulation and FLIPD computation in Section 2.2, including Equation 16, are unchanged. Added explanations do not alter the estimator or its procedure.

E1.justification: Neither version conducts training or evaluation on datasets or test scenarios. Application examples remain background discussion.

E2.justification: Neither version evaluates comparison methods against FLIPD. The additional cited works are literature context, not newly evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: Neither version reports an experimental evaluation protocol, data splits, training budgets, or evaluation metrics. The added error-bound discussion concerns future theoretical work.

E4.justification: Neither version reports ablations, robustness tests, sensitivity studies, or case studies. Appendices A and B retain the same mathematical proofs.

E5.justification: Repeated-run information, seeds, empirical uncertainty estimates, confidence intervals, and significance tests are absent from both versions.

E6.justification: No original experimental results are added, removed, or revised. Existing statements about FLIPD's performance and occasional negative estimates remain attributed to Kamkari et al. (2024b).

T1.justification: The theorem assumptions, statements, supporting propositions, and proofs in Section 5 and Appendices A and B are unchanged. Explicit covariance notation restates the existing Gaussian definition, and the expanded future-work discussion supplies no new formal error bound or derivation.

C1.justification: Both versions claim the same theoretical justification of FLIPD beyond affine manifolds and the analogous uniform-convolution result linking intrinsic dimension to ball probabilities. Their scope and regularity assumptions remain unchanged.

C2.justification: Section 6 expands v1's general proposal to quantify score-approximation error. v2 explains that controlling FLIPD's error would require bounds on both score and score-Jacobian approximation, and identifies the latter as an unresolved direction.

D1.justification: No implementation, hyperparameter, hardware, runtime, or code/data access information is added or revised. The new OpenReview information concerns publication rather than reproducibility resources.

R1.justification: v2 adds six references: Chen et al. (2023, 2024), Oko et al. (2023), Tang and Yang (2024), Wang et al. (2024), and Ventura et al. (2025). A new Section 3 paragraph discusses manifold recovery, finite-sample diffusion theory, and score-Jacobian structure, extending context without redefining the contribution.

P1.justification: v2 adds short clarifications in Section 2, a related-work paragraph, and an expanded ending to Section 6. Publication information is added, while section order and most prose remain unchanged.

P2.justification: v2 adds TMLR running headers and first-page review information, with accompanying spacing and page-break changes. Both retain the same single-column presentation and contain no figures or tables.

improvement.justification: The expanded Section 6 makes v1's general discussion of estimation error more specific by identifying the missing score-Jacobian error control. Together with broader related-work context, this improves clarity and usefulness modestly while leaving the core theoretical results and proofs unchanged.
